title: Cloning Vectors in Bacterial and Yeast Systems, with Extensions to Mammalian Cells: A Comparative Framework for Architecture, Performance and Design
content: Cloning-vector performance emerges from the interaction of DNA cargo, vector architecture, host physiology and the intended experimental task. This narrative Review compares major bacterial and yeast cloning systems, including plasmids, bacteriophage-derived vectors, cosmids, phagemids, fosmids, bacterial and P1-derived artificial chromosomes, yeast plasmid families, yeast artificial chromosomes and shuttle platforms; mammalian chromosome-scale systems are considered as a focused extension. Rather than ranking vectors by nominal insert capacity, this Review examines cargo accommodation, replication, copy-number control, structural integrity, segregation, host compatibility, burden and workflow requirements. Particular attention is given to the distinct maintenance logic of Saccharomyces cerevisiae YEp, YCp and YIp vectors and to emerging episomal and chromosome-based systems in Komagataella phaffii. This Review proposes a revised Vector Performance and Design Framework (VPDF) that separates non-negotiable requirements from preferred performance targets, evaluates vector–host–cargo combinations across independent dimensions, and grades the evidence supporting each judgement. Worked examples show how the framework can structure decisions; they are not independent validation. It also sets out practical quality-assurance requirements: sequence-level verification, copy-number measurement and longitudinal assessment of clone retention. Drawing on both historical foundations and recent experimental evidence, this Review argues that vector choice is a context-specific engineering decision, not a capacity-based lookup.
